job.style: a news-style report about a real-world situation

response.passage: In a recent experiment, a new AI system was trained to identify medical images by processing thousands of X-ray scans. Unlike simple computer programs that follow a rigid list of pre-written rules, this AI learned by identifying patterns within the data it was shown. However, the system struggled when it encountered images from a different hospital with slightly different lighting. This revealed that an AI is not a universal genius; a system excellent at medical diagnosis cannot automatically drive a car or write poetry. Furthermore, researchers discovered that because the training data mostly featured patients from one specific demographic, the AI became less accurate for other groups. This bias was not caused by a programmer intentionally writing unfair code, but by the limited variety in the data itself. Even when the AI confidently presented its findings in a professional report, some of its conclusions were factually incorrect. This proves that an AI’s output is not guaranteed to be true just because it sounds authoritative or because it has been trained on a large dataset. Users must remember that AI systems are tools that learn from examples, and their performance depends entirely on the quality and diversity of the information they are given.
response.summary: AI systems learn by identifying patterns in data rather than following fixed rules. Because they are limited by their training data, they can be biased and make mistakes despite sounding confident.
